content.prompt:
In the isosceles trapezium $ABCD$, $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $F$ is the midpoint of $CD$. Prove that $EF\perp DC$.

(Hint: Join $AF$ and $BF$.)

spec.description: Isosceles trapezium with parallel top and bottom and equal-leg ticks. E, F and all hinted construction segments remain absent. Ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel DC; AD=BC; AB is the shorter base.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied scaffold only; no construction or conclusion is shown.

answer.short: $\triangle ADF\equiv\triangle BCF$ (SAS), so $AF=BF$. The median $FE$ of isosceles triangle $AFB$ is perpendicular to $AB$; since $AB\parallel DC$, $EF\perp DC$.
answer.worked:
Join $AF$ and $BF$. First establish the equal base angles: choose $X$ on $DC$ with $BX\parallel AD$. Then $ABXD$ is a parallelogram, so $BX=AD=BC$. Thus triangle $BXC$ is isosceles, giving $\angle BXC=\angle BCX$. Corresponding angles give $\angle ADC=\angle BXC$, hence $\angle ADF=\angle BCF$.

In triangles $ADF$ and $BCF$:
$$\begin{align*}
AD&=BC &&\text{(isosceles trapezium)}\\
DF&=CF &&\text{(}F\text{ is the midpoint of }CD\text{)}\\
\angle ADF&=\angle BCF &&\text{(equal base angles).}
\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle ADF\equiv\triangle BCF$ (SAS), so $AF=BF$.

In triangles $AEF$ and $BEF$, $AE=BE$ (midpoint), $AF=BF$, and $EF=EF$ (common). Thus $\triangle AEF\equiv\triangle BEF$ (SSS), giving $\angle AEF=\angle BEF$. These adjacent angles sum to $180^\circ$, so each is $90^\circ$. Hence $EF\perp AB$. Since $AB\parallel DC$, $EF\perp DC$.
